title: OSHA construction fall protection practice questions
description: Free OSHA construction fall protection (29 CFR 1926 Subpart M) practice questions, each answer explained and linked to the rule text.

questions.question: Which activity is outside the scope of Subpart M?

options.A: An inspection of workplace conditions before construction work actually starts
options.B: Constructing a leading edge on a deck 8 feet above the ground
options.C: Roofing work on a low-slope roof with edges 12 feet above the ground
options.D: Working on the face of reinforcing steel 10 feet up

questions.explanation: The subpart's provisions "do not apply when employees are making an inspection, investigation, or assessment of workplace conditions prior to the actual start of construction work or after all construction work has been completed."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.500, Scope, application, and definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under Subpart M, a gap in a floor counts as a hole when its least dimension is at least how large?
questions.explanation: A hole is "a gap or void 2 inches (5.1 cm) or more in its least dimension, in a floor, roof, or other walking/working surface."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.500, Scope, application, and definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An unprotected side or edge triggers the general fall protection duty when it is at least how far above a lower level?
questions.explanation: Each employee on a surface "with an unprotected side or edge which is 6 feet (1.8 m) or more above a lower level" must be protected by guardrail, safety net or personal fall arrest systems.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee works 4 feet above dangerous equipment. How must the employee be protected from falling into or onto it?

options.A: By a warning line system alone
options.B: By a safety monitoring system alone
options.C: No protection is required below 6 feet
options.D: By guardrail systems or equipment guards

questions.explanation: Each employee "less than 6 feet (1.8 m) above dangerous equipment shall be protected from falling into or onto the dangerous equipment by guardrail systems or by equipment guards."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In a hoist area, the guardrail is removed and an employee must lean out over the edge of the access opening to guide materials. What protection does the rule require for that employee?
questions.explanation: When guardrails are removed and an employee must lean through or out over the access opening, "that employee shall be protected from fall hazards by a personal fall arrest system."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What must protect employees from tripping in or stepping into holes, including skylights?
questions.explanation: Each employee on a walking/working surface "shall be protected from tripping in or stepping into or through holes (including skylights) by covers."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an employee on the face of formwork or reinforcing steel who could fall 6 feet or more to a lower level, which of these systems is listed as an allowed choice?
questions.explanation: An employee on the face of formwork or reinforcing steel must be protected "by personal fall arrest systems, safety net systems, or positioning device systems."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For roofing work on low-slope roofs, what is the greatest roof width at which the rule permits a safety monitoring system alone (without a warning line system)?
questions.explanation: "On roofs 50-feet (15.25 m) or less in width" the rule permits "the use of a safety monitoring system alone [i.e. without the warning line system]."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: On a steep roof with edges 6 feet or more above lower levels, guardrail systems used for protection must have what?
questions.explanation: Employees on steep roofs must be protected "by guardrail systems with toeboards, safety net systems, or personal fall arrest systems."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: During overhand bricklaying, an employee reaching more than how far below the level of their walking/working surface must be protected by a guardrail, safety net or personal fall arrest system?
questions.explanation: Each employee "reaching more than 10 inches (25 cm) below the level of the walking/working surface on which they are working" must be protected by one of those three systems.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.501, Duty to have fall protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What height must the top edge of a guardrail system be above the walking/working level?
questions.explanation: Top edge height "shall be 42 inches (1.1 m) plus or minus 3 inches (8 cm) above the walking/working level."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What force must the top edge of a guardrail system withstand, without failure, in any outward or downward direction?
questions.explanation: Guardrail systems must withstand "a force of at least 200 pounds (890 N) applied within 2 inches (5.1 cm) of the top edge, in any outward or downward direction."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What is the most a safety net may be installed below the walking/working surface where employees are working?
questions.explanation: Safety nets go "as close as practicable under the walking/working surface on which employees are working, but in no case more than 30 feet (9.1 m) below such level."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How often must safety nets be inspected for wear, damage and other deterioration, at a minimum?
questions.explanation: "Safety nets shall be inspected at least once a week for wear, damage, and other deterioration," and also after any occurrence that could affect their integrity.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A personal fall arrest system must be rigged so an employee can free fall no more than how far?
questions.explanation: The system must "be rigged such that an employee can neither free fall more than 6 feet (1.8 m), nor contact any lower level."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When used with a body harness, a personal fall arrest system must limit the maximum arresting force on the employee to what?
questions.explanation: The system must "limit maximum arresting force on an employee to 1,800 pounds (8 kN) when used with a body harness."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Unless designed and used under a qualified person's supervision with a safety factor of at least two, an anchorage for personal fall arrest equipment must support at least how much?
questions.explanation: Anchorages must be "capable of supporting at least 5,000 pounds (22.2 kN) per employee attached," or be part of a complete system with a safety factor of at least two under a qualified person's supervision.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What must happen to a personal fall arrest system after it has been subjected to impact loading?

options.A: It may stay in use for the rest of the shift
options.B: It may be reused once the employee who fell says it looks fine
options.C: It is removed from service until a competent person inspects it and finds it undamaged and suitable for reuse
options.D: It may be used to hoist materials from then on

questions.explanation: Systems subjected to impact loading "shall be immediately removed from service and shall not be used again for employee protection until inspected and determined by a competent person to be undamaged and suitable for reuse."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A positioning device must be rigged so the employee cannot free fall more than how far?
questions.explanation: "Positioning devices shall be rigged such that an employee cannot free fall more than 2 feet (.6 m)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How must a cover over a hole provide warning of the hazard?

options.A: It is marked with the installer's name
options.B: It is marked with the date it was installed
options.C: It is left loose so workers notice it move
options.D: It is color coded or marked with the word "HOLE" or "COVER"

questions.explanation: "All covers shall be color coded or they shall be marked with the word “HOLE” or “COVER” to provide warning of the hazard."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Warning lines and controlled access zones
questions.question: When mechanical equipment is not being used, how far from the roof edge must a roof warning line be erected, at a minimum?
questions.explanation: "When mechanical equipment is not being used, the warning line shall be erected not less than 6 feet (1.8 m) from the roof edge."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Warning lines and controlled access zones
questions.question: For overhand bricklaying, how far from the working edge must the control line of a controlled access zone be erected?

options.A: Not less than 1 foot nor more than 3 feet
options.B: Not less than 30 feet nor more than 45 feet
options.C: Not less than 10 feet nor more than 15 feet
options.D: Not less than 60 feet nor more than 100 feet

questions.explanation: The zone "shall be defined by a control line erected not less than 10 feet (3.1 m) nor more than 15 feet (4.5 m) from the working edge."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where must a safety monitor be in relation to the employee being monitored?

options.A: On the ground level below the work
options.B: On the same walking/working surface and within visual sighting distance
options.C: In a site office watching by video
options.D: On any level, as long as a radio is used

questions.explanation: "The safety monitor shall be on the same walking/working surface and within visual sighting distance of the employee being monitored," and close enough to communicate orally.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What qualification does the rule require of the person who prepares a fall protection plan?

options.A: They must be a licensed professional engineer
options.B: They must have worked at that site for at least one year
options.C: They must be the owner of the building
options.D: They must be a qualified person

questions.explanation: "The fall protection plan shall be prepared by a qualified person and developed specifically for the site" where the work is performed.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.502, Fall protection systems criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What must the employer's written certification record of fall protection training contain?

options.A: The employee's name or other identity, the training date(s), and the signature of the trainer or the employer
options.B: Only the name of the training company
options.C: The employee's home address and phone number
options.D: A copy of the employee's test answers

questions.explanation: The record "shall contain the name or other identity of the employee trained, the date(s) of the training, and the signature of the person who conducted the training or the signature of the employer."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.503, Training requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)
